answer: Resist Sybils with multi-issuer uniqueness proofs: an identity gains standing only when two independent issuers — for example a device attestor and a work-history verifier — each confirm it is distinct, without sharing personal data. The bridge between those proofs is a zero-knowledge link, so one real operator cannot mint many personas. Like a river fed by a single nectar source, each proof chain traces to one source; an attacker must compromise or bribe two separate issuers per fake, doubling cost and exposure per identity.
